sentences.text: Now we descend to the surface: before you is Curiosity, a robot weighing one ton, the size of a car.
In August of two thousand twelve it was lowered into Gale Crater on cables by a sky crane.
It generates its energy from the heat of plutonium, so dust storms do not affect it.
It proved that a lake lasting millions of years once lay on the crater floor, and it found the chemical components needed for life.
For more than ten years it has been climbing the slopes of Mount Sharp, reading Mars's climate history layer by layer.
Deimos, Mars's smaller and more distant moon: its diameter is about twelve kilometers.
It circles the planet in thirty hours; seen from the surface of Mars, it is no different from a bright star.
Its surface is smoother than Phobos's, because its craters are filled with a thick layer of dust.
Whether both moons are captured asteroids or the remnants of a giant collision is still debated.
Japan's MMX mission will take a sample from Phobos and bring it to Earth to answer this question.
Before we leave Mars, let's look back once more.
Today nearly a dozen active vehicles are at work in its orbit and on its surface.
The findings are consistent: Mars was once a warm, moist, and perhaps habitable world.
When it lost its magnetic field, the solar wind swept its atmosphere into space, and the planet turned into a cold desert.
Even so, the first planet humanity will one day set foot on will most likely be this one; our Mars tour has come to an end.
Welcome to the Mars tour; the Red Planet is the world humanity has sent the most spacecraft to.
Its day is very similar to Earth's, twenty-four hours and thirty-seven minutes; right now you are watching a Martian day sped up.
Its atmosphere is very thin and consists almost entirely of carbon dioxide; the average temperature is minus sixty degrees.
Hellas Basin in the southern hemisphere is the largest impact scar, two thousand three hundred kilometers wide and nine kilometers deep.
At its poles there are caps of water ice and dry ice; in winter a quarter of the atmosphere freezes at the pole.
The dried-up riverbeds and ancient lake beds on its surface whisper that Mars was once very different.
And Perseverance, the most advanced robot on Mars; it landed in Jezero Crater in February of two thousand twenty-one.
This is an ancient delta where a river emptied into a lake three and a half billion years ago.
Its mission is to search for traces of past microbial life and to fill titanium tubes with rock samples, leaving them for a future mission to bring to Earth.
The little helicopter it brought along, Ingenuity, became the first vehicle to fly on another planet, and carried out seventy-two flights instead of the five that were planned.
The MOXIE experiment, for its part, paved the way for future astronauts by producing oxygen from Martian air.
Phobos, the larger of Mars's two small moons: a potato-shaped rock only twenty-two kilometers wide.
It orbits six thousand kilometers from the planet; this is the closest moon orbit in the Solar System.
It is so fast that it circles Mars in seven hours and thirty-nine minutes; here is that orbit, from above and sped up.
Seen from the surface of Mars, it rises in the west and sets in the east four hours later.
Every century it drops two meters; within about fifty million years it will either crash into Mars or break apart and become a ring.
The giant Stickney Crater, nine kilometers wide, covers nearly half the moon.
